messages:
support: Customer (acct: acme-corp) in Private/VPC deployment reporting missing audit entries for key-wrapping ops and intermittent 403 from our KMS proxy. Ticket #INC-8782. Can eng-security triage?

alex: thanks — any repro steps they ran? did they rotate keys recently?

support: customer ran a replay of a create-encryption-key -> encrypt -> decrypt sequence against our private KMS endpoint. Occasionally decrypt returns 403 and we have no corresponding audit log entry in the retention store for that key id. Happens ~2x/day.

sanam: do they use HSM-backed keys or software keys? we need to know if key-wrap happens inside HSM (no audit event emitted if it never reached control plane?)

support: they say HSM-backed (external HSM via partner HSM-A). They provided these snippets: 
```
# repro (from inside their app subnet)
curl -i -X POST https://kms.private.redwood/acme/v1/crypto/decrypt 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 
  -d '{"key_id":"kk-1234","ciphertext":"..."}'
```
response: sometimes `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` with body `{"error":"insufficient_scope"}`
```

alex: ok. 403 + "insufficient_scope" suggests our auth proxy rejected the JWT or it couldn't validate key policy. But missing audit logs is concerning — we should check our audit-forwarder and the VPC egress path to the retention SIEM.

irfan: I can check network flows. customer VPC details? subnet IDs and whether they run with NAT gateway or egress-only IGW? If egress gets SNAT'd we might see traffic come from different IPs at our infra side and dedup may miss events.

support: they use a NAT instance (old setup) in the private subnet. Subnets: sn-0a1b2c, sn-0d2e3f. They use AWS PrivateLink to talk to our control plane, not internet egress.

sanam: PrivateLink + NAT instance is odd — need to confirm which path for audit ingestion. Also, HSM partner uses mutual TLS to our HSM proxy; that traffic must be allowed on port 15001 between their HSM gateway and our HSM endpoint. If firewall blocks intermittently we could see 403s at the proxy.

alex: can we get the customer's kube/host TCP dumps around an incident time? even just conntrack logs or `curl -v` output showing TLS handshake failing vs auth rejection.

support: attached logs from 2026-03-10T02:14Z (they included connection resets and `alert: tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake`).

irfan: that points to middlebox (NAT instance) sometimes mangling the stream -> HSM handshake fails -> our proxy rejects -> 403 surfaced to app. That would also explain missing audit entry because the key op never reached the KMS control plane.

compliance: note we need to document retention implication: if audit events never reached retention store, this could be a data-retention gap for regulated customers. Customer asked for 30d immutable retention. Need to confirm whether events were ever emitted from runtime.

alex: next steps: (1) eng-ops (irfan) to validate network path and NAT instance logs during incident windows, (2) devex/supp to get targeted tcpdump or `openssl s_client -connect <hsm-host>:15001 -servername <hsm-host>` output from customer, (3) infra to check audit-forwarder logs for dropped/failed posts and S3 put errors, (4) compliance to prepare customer-facing statement if gap confirmed. Owners: irfan, sanam, alex, compliance. ETA: initial findings in 48h.

irfan: I'll pull VPC flow logs + NAT instance syslogs for the windows and post summary here. Expecting to test for TCP RSTs and TLS truncation.

sanam: I'll reach out to HSM partner to see if they show any client cert handshake failures for acme-corp's HSM gateway.

support: pinging customer for `openssl s_client` output and pcap, they said okay and will send by EOD PST.

security-bot: :eyes: alert created -> SEV2 if retention gap confirmed. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-8782

alex: small troubleshooting command customers can run (shareable):
```
# test TLS & HTTP path to our KMS proxy from app host
openssl s_client -connect hsm-gw.acme.internal:15001 -servername hsm-gw.acme.internal -brief
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://kms.private.redwood/acme/v1/crypto/decrypt -d '{}'
```
If TLS fails, likely middlebox. If TLS OK but 403, capture full response headers and token claims.

compliance: please note we must capture the timeline and any missing retention windows for legal. If audit-forwarder shows transient 5xx or credential issues, escalate to platform-ops for hotfix.

support: customer uploaded pcap snippet (linked in ticket). I'll attach to this thread when I have it. TY all. :pray:
